scene.label: Act 3, Scene 5
scene.title: SCENE V. Another part of the Forest

lines.text: Sweet Phoebe, do not scorn me, do not, Phoebe.
lines.plainText: Sweet Phoebe do not scorn me do not Phoebe

lines.text: Say that you love me not, but say not so
lines.plainText: Say that you love me not but say not so

lines.text: In bitterness. The common executioner,
lines.plainText: In bitterness The common executioner

lines.text: Whose heart th' accustomed sight of death makes hard,
lines.plainText: Whose heart th' accustomed sight of death makes hard

lines.text: Falls not the axe upon the humbled neck
lines.plainText: Falls not the axe upon the humbled neck

lines.text: But first begs pardon. Will you sterner be
lines.plainText: But first begs pardon Will you sterner be

lines.text: Than he that dies and lives by bloody drops?
lines.plainText: Than he that dies and lives by bloody drops

content.text: Enter Rosalind, Celia and Corin, at a distance.

lines.text: I would not be thy executioner;
lines.plainText: I would not be thy executioner

lines.text: I fly thee, for I would not injure thee.
lines.plainText: I fly thee for I would not injure thee

lines.text: Thou tell'st me there is murder in mine eye.
lines.plainText: Thou tell'st me there is murder in mine eye

lines.text: 'Tis pretty, sure, and very probable
lines.plainText: 'Tis pretty sure and very probable

lines.text: That eyes, that are the frail'st and softest things,
lines.plainText: That eyes that are the frail'st and softest things

lines.text: Who shut their coward gates on atomies,
lines.plainText: Who shut their coward gates on atomies

lines.text: Should be called tyrants, butchers, murderers.
lines.plainText: Should be called tyrants butchers murderers

lines.text: Now I do frown on thee with all my heart,
lines.plainText: Now I do frown on thee with all my heart

lines.text: And if mine eyes can wound, now let them kill thee.
lines.plainText: And if mine eyes can wound now let them kill thee

lines.text: Now counterfeit to swoon; why, now fall down;
lines.plainText: Now counterfeit to swoon why now fall down

lines.text: Or if thou canst not, O, for shame, for shame,
lines.plainText: Or if thou canst not O for shame for shame

lines.text: Lie not, to say mine eyes are murderers.
lines.plainText: Lie not to say mine eyes are murderers

lines.text: Now show the wound mine eye hath made in thee.
lines.plainText: Now show the wound mine eye hath made in thee

lines.text: Scratch thee but with a pin, and there remains
lines.plainText: Scratch thee but with a pin and there remains

lines.text: Some scar of it; lean upon a rush,
lines.plainText: Some scar of it lean upon a rush

lines.text: The cicatrice and capable impressure
lines.plainText: The cicatrice and capable impressure

lines.text: Thy palm some moment keeps. But now mine eyes,
lines.plainText: Thy palm some moment keeps But now mine eyes

lines.text: Which I have darted at thee, hurt thee not;
lines.plainText: Which I have darted at thee hurt thee not

lines.text: Nor I am sure there is not force in eyes
lines.plainText: Nor I am sure there is not force in eyes

lines.text: That can do hurt.
lines.plainText: That can do hurt

lines.text: O dear Phoebe,
lines.plainText: O dear Phoebe

lines.text: If ever—as that ever may be near—
lines.plainText: If everas that ever may be near

lines.text: You meet in some fresh cheek the power of fancy,
lines.plainText: You meet in some fresh cheek the power of fancy

lines.text: Then shall you know the wounds invisible
lines.plainText: Then shall you know the wounds invisible

lines.text: That love's keen arrows make.
lines.plainText: That love's keen arrows make

lines.text: But till that time
lines.plainText: But till that time

lines.text: Come not thou near me. And when that time comes,
lines.plainText: Come not thou near me And when that time comes

lines.text: Afflict me with thy mocks, pity me not,
lines.plainText: Afflict me with thy mocks pity me not

lines.text: As till that time I shall not pity thee.
lines.plainText: As till that time I shall not pity thee

lines.text: [Advancing.] And why, I pray you? Who might be your mother,
lines.plainText: Advancing And why I pray you Who might be your mother

lines.text: That you insult, exult, and all at once,
lines.plainText: That you insult exult and all at once

lines.text: Over the wretched? What though you have no beauty—
lines.plainText: Over the wretched What though you have no beauty

lines.text: As, by my faith, I see no more in you
lines.plainText: As by my faith I see no more in you

lines.text: Than without candle may go dark to bed—
lines.plainText: Than without candle may go dark to bed

lines.text: Must you be therefore proud and pitiless?
lines.plainText: Must you be therefore proud and pitiless

lines.text: Why, what means this? Why do you look on me?
lines.plainText: Why what means this Why do you look on me

lines.text: I see no more in you than in the ordinary
lines.plainText: I see no more in you than in the ordinary

lines.text: Of nature's sale-work. 'Od's my little life,
lines.plainText: Of nature's salework 'Od's my little life

lines.text: I think she means to tangle my eyes too!
lines.plainText: I think she means to tangle my eyes too

lines.text: No, faith, proud mistress, hope not after it.
lines.plainText: No faith proud mistress hope not after it

lines.text: 'Tis not your inky brows, your black silk hair,
lines.plainText: 'Tis not your inky brows your black silk hair

lines.text: Your bugle eyeballs, nor your cheek of cream,
lines.plainText: Your bugle eyeballs nor your cheek of cream

lines.text: That can entame my spirits to your worship.
lines.plainText: That can entame my spirits to your worship

lines.text: You foolish shepherd, wherefore do you follow her,
lines.plainText: You foolish shepherd wherefore do you follow her

lines.text: Like foggy south, puffing with wind and rain?
lines.plainText: Like foggy south puffing with wind and rain

lines.text: You are a thousand times a properer man
lines.plainText: You are a thousand times a properer man

lines.text: Than she a woman. 'Tis such fools as you
lines.plainText: Than she a woman 'Tis such fools as you

lines.text: That makes the world full of ill-favoured children.
lines.plainText: That makes the world full of illfavoured children

lines.text: 'Tis not her glass but you that flatters her,
lines.plainText: 'Tis not her glass but you that flatters her

lines.text: And out of you she sees herself more proper
lines.plainText: And out of you she sees herself more proper

lines.text: Than any of her lineaments can show her.
lines.plainText: Than any of her lineaments can show her

lines.text: But, mistress, know yourself; down on your knees,
lines.plainText: But mistress know yourself down on your knees

lines.text: And thank heaven, fasting, for a good man's love.
lines.plainText: And thank heaven fasting for a good man's love

lines.text: For I must tell you friendly in your ear,
lines.plainText: For I must tell you friendly in your ear

lines.text: Sell when you can; you are not for all markets.
lines.plainText: Sell when you can you are not for all markets

lines.text: Cry the man mercy, love him, take his offer;
lines.plainText: Cry the man mercy love him take his offer

lines.text: Foul is most foul, being foul to be a scoffer.
lines.plainText: Foul is most foul being foul to be a scoffer

lines.text: So take her to thee, shepherd. Fare you well.
lines.plainText: So take her to thee shepherd Fare you well

lines.text: Sweet youth, I pray you chide a year together!
lines.plainText: Sweet youth I pray you chide a year together

lines.text: I had rather hear you chide than this man woo.
lines.plainText: I had rather hear you chide than this man woo

lines.text: He's fall'n in love with your foulness, and she'll fall in love with my anger. If it be so, as fast as she answers thee with frowning looks, I'll sauce her with bitter words. Why look you so upon me?
lines.plainText: He's fall'n in love with your foulness and she'll fall in love with my anger If it be so as fast as she answers thee with frowning looks I'll sauce her with bitter words Why look you so upon me

lines.text: For no ill will I bear you.
lines.plainText: For no ill will I bear you

lines.text: I pray you do not fall in love with me,
lines.plainText: I pray you do not fall in love with me

lines.text: For I am falser than vows made in wine.
lines.plainText: For I am falser than vows made in wine

lines.text: Besides, I like you not. If you will know my house,
lines.plainText: Besides I like you not If you will know my house

lines.text: 'Tis at the tuft of olives here hard by.
lines.plainText: 'Tis at the tuft of olives here hard by

lines.text: Will you go, sister? Shepherd, ply her hard.
lines.plainText: Will you go sister Shepherd ply her hard

lines.text: Come, sister. Shepherdess, look on him better,
lines.plainText: Come sister Shepherdess look on him better

lines.text: And be not proud. Though all the world could see,
lines.plainText: And be not proud Though all the world could see

lines.text: None could be so abused in sight as he.
lines.plainText: None could be so abused in sight as he

lines.text: Come, to our flock.
lines.plainText: Come to our flock

lines.text: Dead shepherd, now I find thy saw of might:
lines.plainText: Dead shepherd now I find thy saw of might

lines.text: "Who ever loved that loved not at first sight?"
lines.plainText: Who ever loved that loved not at first sight

lines.text: Sweet Phoebe—
lines.plainText: Sweet Phoebe

lines.text: Ha, what sayst thou, Silvius?
lines.plainText: Ha what sayst thou Silvius

lines.text: Sweet Phoebe, pity me.
lines.plainText: Sweet Phoebe pity me

lines.text: Why, I am sorry for thee, gentle Silvius.
lines.plainText: Why I am sorry for thee gentle Silvius

lines.text: Wherever sorrow is, relief would be.
lines.plainText: Wherever sorrow is relief would be

lines.text: If you do sorrow at my grief in love,
lines.plainText: If you do sorrow at my grief in love

lines.text: By giving love your sorrow and my grief
lines.plainText: By giving love your sorrow and my grief

lines.text: Were both extermined.
lines.plainText: Were both extermined

lines.text: Thou hast my love. Is not that neighbourly?
lines.plainText: Thou hast my love Is not that neighbourly

lines.text: I would have you.
lines.plainText: I would have you

lines.text: Why, that were covetousness.
lines.plainText: Why that were covetousness

lines.text: Silvius, the time was that I hated thee;
lines.plainText: Silvius the time was that I hated thee

lines.text: And yet it is not that I bear thee love;
lines.plainText: And yet it is not that I bear thee love

lines.text: But since that thou canst talk of love so well,
lines.plainText: But since that thou canst talk of love so well

lines.text: Thy company, which erst was irksome to me,
lines.plainText: Thy company which erst was irksome to me

lines.text: I will endure, and I'll employ thee too.
lines.plainText: I will endure and I'll employ thee too

lines.text: But do not look for further recompense
lines.plainText: But do not look for further recompense

lines.text: Than thine own gladness that thou art employed.
lines.plainText: Than thine own gladness that thou art employed

lines.text: So holy and so perfect is my love,
lines.plainText: So holy and so perfect is my love

lines.text: And I in such a poverty of grace,
lines.plainText: And I in such a poverty of grace

lines.text: That I shall think it a most plenteous crop
lines.plainText: That I shall think it a most plenteous crop

lines.text: To glean the broken ears after the man
lines.plainText: To glean the broken ears after the man

lines.text: That the main harvest reaps. Loose now and then
lines.plainText: That the main harvest reaps Loose now and then

lines.text: A scattered smile, and that I'll live upon.
lines.plainText: A scattered smile and that I'll live upon

lines.text: Know'st thou the youth that spoke to me erewhile?
lines.plainText: Know'st thou the youth that spoke to me erewhile

lines.text: Not very well, but I have met him oft,
lines.plainText: Not very well but I have met him oft

lines.text: And he hath bought the cottage and the bounds
lines.plainText: And he hath bought the cottage and the bounds

lines.text: That the old carlot once was master of.
lines.plainText: That the old carlot once was master of

lines.text: Think not I love him, though I ask for him.
lines.plainText: Think not I love him though I ask for him

lines.text: 'Tis but a peevish boy—yet he talks well.
lines.plainText: 'Tis but a peevish boyyet he talks well

lines.text: But what care I for words? Yet words do well
lines.plainText: But what care I for words Yet words do well

lines.text: When he that speaks them pleases those that hear.
lines.plainText: When he that speaks them pleases those that hear

lines.text: It is a pretty youth—not very pretty—
lines.plainText: It is a pretty youthnot very pretty

lines.text: But sure he's proud, and yet his pride becomes him.
lines.plainText: But sure he's proud and yet his pride becomes him

lines.text: He'll make a proper man. The best thing in him
lines.plainText: He'll make a proper man The best thing in him

lines.text: Is his complexion; and faster than his tongue
lines.plainText: Is his complexion and faster than his tongue

lines.text: Did make offence, his eye did heal it up.
lines.plainText: Did make offence his eye did heal it up

lines.text: He is not very tall, yet for his years he's tall;
lines.plainText: He is not very tall yet for his years he's tall

lines.text: His leg is but so-so, and yet 'tis well.
lines.plainText: His leg is but soso and yet 'tis well

lines.text: There was a pretty redness in his lip,
lines.plainText: There was a pretty redness in his lip

lines.text: A little riper and more lusty red
lines.plainText: A little riper and more lusty red

lines.text: Than that mixed in his cheek. 'Twas just the difference
lines.plainText: Than that mixed in his cheek 'Twas just the difference

lines.text: Betwixt the constant red and mingled damask.
lines.plainText: Betwixt the constant red and mingled damask

lines.text: There be some women, Silvius, had they marked him
lines.plainText: There be some women Silvius had they marked him

lines.text: In parcels as I did, would have gone near
lines.plainText: In parcels as I did would have gone near

lines.text: To fall in love with him; but for my part
lines.plainText: To fall in love with him but for my part

lines.text: I love him not nor hate him not; and yet
lines.plainText: I love him not nor hate him not and yet

lines.text: I have more cause to hate him than to love him.
lines.plainText: I have more cause to hate him than to love him

lines.text: For what had he to do to chide at me?
lines.plainText: For what had he to do to chide at me

lines.text: He said mine eyes were black and my hair black,
lines.plainText: He said mine eyes were black and my hair black

lines.text: And now I am remembered, scorned at me.
lines.plainText: And now I am remembered scorned at me

lines.text: I marvel why I answered not again.
lines.plainText: I marvel why I answered not again

lines.text: But that's all one: omittance is no quittance.
lines.plainText: But that's all one omittance is no quittance

lines.text: I'll write to him a very taunting letter,
lines.plainText: I'll write to him a very taunting letter

lines.text: And thou shalt bear it. Wilt thou, Silvius?
lines.plainText: And thou shalt bear it Wilt thou Silvius

lines.text: Phoebe, with all my heart.
lines.plainText: Phoebe with all my heart

lines.text: I'll write it straight,
lines.plainText: I'll write it straight

lines.text: The matter's in my head and in my heart.
lines.plainText: The matter's in my head and in my heart

lines.text: I will be bitter with him and passing short.
lines.plainText: I will be bitter with him and passing short

lines.text: Go with me, Silvius.
lines.plainText: Go with me Silvius
